abstract_summary: The YOLO series has become the most popular framework for real-time object detection due to its reasonable trade-off between speed and accuracy. However, we observe that the speed and accuracy of YOLOs are negatively affected by the NMS. Recently, end-to-end Transformer-based detectors (DETRs) have provided an alter...

evidence.excerpt:
To enable a fair comparison of the end-to-end speed of var-
ious real-time detectors, we establish an end-to-end speed
benchmark. Considering that the execution time of NMS is
influenced by the input, it is necessary to choose a bench-
mark dataset and calculate the average execution time across
multiple images. We choose COCO val2017 [20] as the
benchmark dataset and append the NMS post-processing
plugin of TensorRT for YOLO detectors as mentioned above.
Specifically, we test the average inference time of the de-
tector according to the NMS thresholds of the correspond-
ing accuracy taken on the benchmark dataset, excluding
I/O and MemoryCopy operations. We utilize the bench-
mark to test the end-to-end speed of anchor-based detectors
YOLOv5 [11] and YOLOv7 [38], as well as anchor-free de-
tectors PP-YOLOE [40], YOLOv6 [16] and YOLOv8

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Headline outcomes are established on external COCO ground-truth annotations and hardware-level TensorRT latency measurements, not on the uncertainty or query-selection signals optimized during training.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Standard COCO val2017 metrics (AP, AP50, AP75, APS/M/L) and TensorRT FP16 latency/FPS measured on T4 GPU.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Supervised training loss combining DETR bounding-box regression and the uncertainty-integrated classification loss against COCO ground-truth labels.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Reported metrics directly support the speed and accuracy advantages claimed over contemporary YOLO variants and prior DETR models, with clear acknowledgement of minor AP degradation on small objects compared to specific YOLO architectures.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The model is evaluated on MS COCO val2017 with standardized metrics (AP, AP50, AP75, APS/M/L) and end-to-end latency benchmarks on T4 GPUs using TensorRT FP16, accompanied by thorough ablation studies confirming each component's utility.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Evaluations rely on standard external ground-truth COCO annotations and hardware-level TensorRT latency measurements across validation sets.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Standard COCO evaluation benchmark metrics (AP, APS, APM, APL) and TensorRT FP16 inference latency on T4 GPU.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Supervised training loss combining standard DETR bounding box regression and uncertainty-integrated classification loss against ground-truth labels.

primary.limitations: The authors explicitly disclose that RT-DETR lags slightly behind strong YOLO baselines (e.g., YOLOv8-L and YOLOv7-X) on small object detection AP (APS).
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is thoroughly detailed, describing the decoupling of intra-scale interactions from cross-scale fusion, the formulation of uncertainty-minimal query selection combining classification and localization discrepancy into the training loss, and flexible speed tuning via decoder layer pruning.
primary.quality_rationale: The study provides clear architectural innovations, transparent experimental controls, comprehensive comparisons against SOTA detectors on a standard benchmark, and detailed ablations validating the hybrid encoder and query selection mechanisms.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper introduces RT-DETR, a real-time end-to-end DETR architecture featuring an efficient hybrid encoder (AIFI and CCFF) and uncertainty-minimal query selection, achieving competitive latency and accuracy trade-offs without NMS post-processing.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The study provides clear architectural innovations, transparent experimental controls, comprehensive comparisons against SOTA detectors on a standard benchmark, and detailed ablations validating the hybrid encoder and query selection mechanisms.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors explicitly disclose that RT-DETR lags slightly behind strong YOLO baselines (e.g., YOLOv8-L and YOLOv7-X) on small object detection AP (APS).
